A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Synth-SBDH study. The main text, figures, tables, and Appendices A–F are readable and can be matched across revisions and relocations.

before.justification: v2 reports original classification, entity-recognition, rationale-distillation, and human/LLM evaluation results, including appendix experiments.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical evaluations and adds FLAN-T5-xl rationale-distillation results in Appendix D.3.2.

M1.justification: The generation, two-stage fine-tuning, and DSS procedures otherwise remain the same. However, Section 3.1 changes from accepting examples with ROUGE-L below 0.7 against every previous example to rejecting examples scoring at least 0.7 against every previous example. These rules are not equivalent; the PDFs do not establish whether this reflects a procedural change or a wording error.

E1.justification: Both versions use Synth-SBDH, MIMIC-SBDHaligned, and VA-SBDH for the same English-language MLC, NER, and DSS tasks. The category regrouping retains the same underlying labels. Testing a larger model adds no dataset, population, or task coverage.

E2.justification: v3 removes all six MIMIC-SBDHaligned pretraining comparator rows from Table 13, although Appendix D.2 still describes that comparison. The new DSS extension includes a standard-fine-tuned FLAN-T5-xl control. RoBERTa rows added to Table 14 repeat comparisons already reported elsewhere.

E3.justification: The added DSS experiment uses a 2.85B-parameter FLAN-T5-xl model trained for 25 epochs, whereas the retained base-model DSS experiments use 100 epochs (Table 12). Existing splits, evaluation metrics, and listed training budgets otherwise remain unchanged; expanded category-mapping explanations document the existing processing.

E4.justification: Appendix D.3.2 adds an examination of rationale utility and performance at a larger model size. Conversely, removing the MIMIC-pretraining rows eliminates numerical evidence for the existing synthetic-versus-real-data ablation. The rare-category analysis, training-size sensitivity experiment, and Appendix E case studies remain.

E5.justification: v3 adds p-values for selected MLC and NER comparisons in Section 5 and cites a statistical reference in Section 4.3. Table 5 newly specifies that DSS entries are means and standard deviations over three independent runs. Other three-run reporting and the existing DSS p-values are retained; no increased run count is established.

E6.justification: Table 14 replaces Llama 3.2 3B MIMIC-SBDHaligned macro-F scores without/with Synth-SBDH from 82.77/91.63 to 88.59/88.33, reversing the reported benefit under the same stated settings. New Table 15 reports FLAN-T5-xl macro-F of 53.67 for standard fine-tuning and 54.58 for DSS. Table 13 loses six control rows. Section 7.2 replaces Patient Disability with Violence among the hardest categories. Table 17 adds percentages, incorrectly reporting 3/258 as 11.63%. Main Tables 3–6 retain their numerical results.

T1.justification: Neither version presents formal theoretical results, proofs, or derivations. The expanded conceptual explanations and category grouping introduce no substantive mathematical development.

C1.justification: The central dataset-release, transfer-performance, rare-category, low-resource, and rationale-distillation claims remain. The headline 63.75% improvement and human-evaluation claims are retained. Reordering the contributions and describing the same label set as 15 categories do not expand the core contribution.

C2.justification: v3 adds specific limitations concerning missing clinical text formats, unverifiable overlap between GPT-4 pretraining and MIMIC-III, and unassessed bias. It distinguishes 13 SBDH categories from pain and transition of care. Appendix C adds deployment and bias-mitigation explanations for two-stage training; Appendix D strengthens the small-model cost argument and revises the interpretation of Llama results.

D1.justification: v3 discloses generation/filtering counts, expands binary category-mapping instructions, specifies a VA-data access route and model checkpoints, and adds annotator coauthorship, residence, and compensation information. Table 12 includes FLAN-T5-xl training and hardware details. Conversely, Section 6 removes the explicit containment criterion previously used to explain relaxed span matching.

R1.justification: v3 adds references supporting significance reporting, sequence-labeling model choices, and clinical bias discussion, including Altman and Bland, InstructUIE, GLiNER, Zack et al., and Omar et al. It removes Mitra et al. (2020) and replaces the Synth-SBDH self-citation with a different Mitra et al. (2025) study. NoteChat's publication update refers to the same work. Overall research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: v3 locally rewrites the methods and results discussion, expands Appendix B's mappings, and subdivides Appendix D.3 into MLC and DSS. It reorders contributions, renames the annotation action Correct to Update, and removes acknowledgments. The overall organization and most appendix prompts, examples, and guidelines remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds the task illustration in Figure 3 and the expanded DSS table, Table 15. Table 1 gains a Labeller column, Table 7 gains category groups, Table 13 loses comparator rows, Table 14 redisplays RoBERTa results, and Table 17 adds percentages. Figures 1 and 2 retain their substantive visual content.

improvement.justification: v3 improves documentation, adds specific limitations and a larger-model DSS evaluation, and reconciles the Llama discussion with revised results. However, v2's numerical controls supporting Appendix D.2 disappear while its comparative conclusion remains. The rewritten filtering rule also creates procedural ambiguity, and Table 17 introduces an incorrect percentage. These gains in explanation and evaluation coexist with weaker verifiability and reporting accuracy, preventing a reliable judgment of net overall improvement.
